### Biography

I am Nga Nguyen, but you can call me Daisy. I am a graduating Senior at Lawrence University, pursuing Physics and Computer Science. I'm currently working on computational plasma physics, and I am aspire to develop high-fidelity models to rigorously study plasma instabilities and turbulence, alongside reduced-order models capable of predicting the real-time onset of instabilities in next-generation fusion systems.

My primary research interests lie broadly in the study of physics, mathematics, computer science, and data science. I believe the tools that each discipline provides are the gifts that we should utilize in the making of science. With a research philosophy rooted in an interdisciplinary approach, my long-term goal is to become a fusion energy research scientist at a national laboratory or a research university, integrating mathematical frameworks, computational methods, and data-driven modeling to develop predictive and computationally efficient tools for understanding and controlling magnetically confined plasma in fusion reactors.

### Personal

I am from Da Nang, Vietnam. A fun fact about me is that I started studying abroad in high school in a small town called Bettendorf, Iowa. I then attended college at Lawrence University in Appleton, Wisconsin. You got it, I have spent a third of my life in the Midwest.

I love playing sports, and some of the sports I enjoy playing is basketball, table tennis, pickleball and volleyball. I started learning how to play basketball and volleyball when I was in Iowa, and I love playing them with friends ever since. Last December, I went to watch my first NBA game with the Lakers in Los Angeles, and it was one of the happiest moments of my life haha.

In college, I also had a chance to take piano lesson "professionally," and I love having a musical outlet to take my time off from working during the day. I also find playing the piano very intellectual and interesting because there is so much that one can unpack from a music piece. I cannot stop from being amazed at not only the musics, but also at the technicality of how my hands interactive with the keyboard could affect the quality of my sound.
